Looking at this problem, I need to find the minimum number of factorials to erase from {1!, 2!, ..., 2017!} so the remaining product is a perfect square.

## Setup

Work over **parity vectors** in F₂: each integer maps to its square-free part (exponent of each prime mod 2). A product is a perfect square iff its parity vector is **0**.

Let **v_k** = parity vector of k!. Let **T** = v₁ + v₂ + ... + v₂₀₁₇ (parity vector of the total product). Erasing a subset S leaves a square iff **∑_{k∈S} v_k = T** (the erased product has the same square-free part as the total). So I need the **minimum-weight subset of {v_k} summing to T**.

## Computing T

Since v_k = w₁ + w₂ + ... + w_k (where w_i = parity vector of i), we get:

$$T = \sum_{k=1}^{2017} v_k = \sum_{i=1}^{2017}(2018 - i)\, w_i$$

Since 2018 is even, (2018 − i) mod 2 = i mod 2, so:

$$T = \sum_{\substack{i \text{ odd} \\ 1 \le i \le 2017}} w_i = \text{sf}(1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdots 2017) = \text{sf}(2017!!)$$

## Zero removals is impossible

2017 is prime (checked: no prime divisor up to √2017 ≈ 44.9). Since 2017 is odd, it appears in 2017!! exactly once (the only odd multiple of 2017 up to 2017 is 2017 itself). So T has coordinate 2017 equal to 1, hence T ≠ 0.

## One removal is impossible

For v_k = T, we need sf(k!) = sf(2017!!). Since T has a 1 in coordinate 2017, we need 2017 | k!, forcing k ≥ 2017, so k = 2017.

Now 2017! = 2017!! · 2016!!, and 2016!! = 2·4·6·...·2016 = 2^{1008} · 1008!. Therefore:

$$\text{sf}(2017!) = \text{sf}(2017!!) \cdot \text{sf}(1008!) = T \cdot \text{sf}(1008!)$$

For v_{2017} = T we'd need sf(1008!) = 1, i.e., 1008! is a perfect square. But **997 is prime** (verified: no prime divisor up to √997 ≈ 31.6), and 997 < 1008 while 2·997 = 1994 > 1008, so 997 appears **exactly once** in 1008!. Thus 1008! is **not** a perfect square, so v_{2017} ≠ T. No single removal works.

## Two removals work

**Claim:** Erasing 1008! and 2017! works, i.e., v_{1008} + v_{2017} = T.

**Proof:**

$$v_{1008} + v_{2017} = \text{sf}(1008!) \oplus \text{sf}(2017!) = \text{sf}(1008!) \oplus \big(T \oplus \text{sf}(1008!)\big) = T \quad \checkmark$$

The remaining product ∏_{k ∉ {1008, 2017}} k! has parity vector T + v_{1008} + v_{2017} = T + T = **0**, so it is a perfect square.

## Conclusion

- **0 removals:** impossible (T ≠ 0).
- **1 removal:** impossible (no v_k equals T).
- **2 removals:** achievable (erase 1008! and 2017!).

The minimum number of factorials that must be erased is $\boxed{2}$.

## Setup

Work over **parity vectors** in F₂: each integer maps to its square-free part (exponent of each prime mod 2). A product is a perfect square iff its parity vector is **0**.

Let **v_k** = parity vector of k!. Let **T** = v₁ + v₂ + ... + v₂₀₁₇ (parity vector of the total product). Erasing a subset S leaves a square iff **∑_{k∈S} v_k = T** (the erased product has the same square-free part as the total). So I need the **minimum-weight subset of {v_k} summing to T**.

## Computing T

Since v_k = w₁ + w₂ + ... + w_k (where w_i = parity vector of i), we get:

$$T = \sum_{k=1}^{2017} v_k = \sum_{i=1}^{2017}(2018 - i)\, w_i$$

Since 2018 is even, (2018 − i) mod 2 = i mod 2, so:

$$T = \sum_{\substack{i \text{ odd} \\ 1 \le i \le 2017}} w_i = \text{sf}(1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdots 2017) = \text{sf}(2017!!)$$

## Zero removals is impossible

2017 is prime (checked: no prime divisor up to √2017 ≈ 44.9). Since 2017 is odd, it appears in 2017!! exactly once (the only odd multiple of 2017 up to 2017 is 2017 itself). So T has coordinate 2017 equal to 1, hence T ≠ 0.

## One removal is impossible

For v_k = T, we need sf(k!) = sf(2017!!). Since T has a 1 in coordinate 2017, we need 2017 | k!, forcing k ≥ 2017, so k = 2017.

Now 2017! = 2017!! · 2016!!, and 2016!! = 2·4·6·...·2016 = 2^{1008} · 1008!. Therefore:

$$\text{sf}(2017!) = \text{sf}(2017!!) \cdot \text{sf}(1008!) = T \cdot \text{sf}(1008!)$$

For v_{2017} = T we'd need sf(1008!) = 1, i.e., 1008! is a perfect square. But **997 is prime** (verified: no prime divisor up to √997 ≈ 31.6), and 997 < 1008 while 2·997 = 1994 > 1008, so 997 appears **exactly once** in 1008!. Thus 1008! is **not** a perfect square, so v_{2017} ≠ T. No single removal works.

## Two removals work

**Claim:** Erasing 1008! and 2017! works, i.e., v_{1008} + v_{2017} = T.

**Proof:**

$$v_{1008} + v_{2017} = \text{sf}(1008!) \oplus \text{sf}(2017!) = \text{sf}(1008!) \oplus \big(T \oplus \text{sf}(1008!)\big) = T \quad \checkmark$$

The remaining product ∏_{k ∉ {1008, 2017}} k! has parity vector T + v_{1008} + v_{2017} = T + T = **0**, so it is a perfect square.

## Conclusion

- **0 removals:** impossible (T ≠ 0).
- **1 removal:** impossible (no v_k equals T).
- **2 removals:** achievable (erase 1008! and 2017!).

The minimum number of factorials that must be erased is $\boxed{2}$.
